name: Parallel & Concurrent Programming
description: Writing correct and fast parallel code: threads and locks, memory models, parallel algorithms, GPUs and MPI.

nodes.name: Why parallel
nodes.desc: The end of frequency scaling, multicore, and concurrency vs parallelism.
nodes.summary: You will understand why hardware moved to multicore and be able to distinguish concurrency from parallelism.
topics: End of Dennard scaling and frequency limits

nodes.name: Amdahl & Gustafson
nodes.desc: Speedup, efficiency, Amdahl's and Gustafson's laws.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute speedup and efficiency and predict scaling limits with Amdahl's and Gustafson's laws.

nodes.name: Parallel models
nodes.desc: Shared memory vs message passing, SIMD vs MIMD and Flynn's taxonomy.
nodes.summary: You will be able to classify parallel systems with Flynn's taxonomy and compare shared-memory and message-passing models.

nodes.name: Threads & locks
nodes.desc: Creating threads, mutexes, condition variables and protecting shared state.
nodes.summary: You will be able to create threads and protect shared state with mutexes and condition variables.

nodes.name: Races & deadlocks
nodes.desc: Data races, deadlocks, livelock and tools for finding them.
nodes.summary: You will be able to identify data races, deadlocks and livelocks and use tools such as thread sanitisers to find them.

nodes.name: Memory models
nodes.desc: Cache coherence, false sharing, memory ordering and happens-before.
nodes.summary: You will understand cache coherence, false sharing and memory ordering well enough to reason about happens-before relationships.

nodes.name: Atomics & lock-free
nodes.desc: Atomic operations, compare-and-swap and lock-free data structures.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use atomic operations and compare-and-swap to build simple lock-free data structures and know their pitfalls.

nodes.name: Concurrent structures
nodes.desc: Concurrent queues, hash maps and fine-grained locking.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design concurrent queues and hash maps using coarse and fine-grained locking strategies.

nodes.name: Tasks & work stealing
nodes.desc: Thread pools, futures, fork-join and work stealing schedulers.
nodes.summary: You will be able to express parallel work as tasks with thread pools, futures and fork-join and explain work stealing.

nodes.name: Actors & async
nodes.desc: Message passing within a process, actors, channels and async I/O.
nodes.summary: You will be able to structure concurrent programs with actors, channels and async I/O instead of shared mutable state.

nodes.name: OpenMP
nodes.desc: Parallel loops, reductions and scheduling with OpenMP.
nodes.summary: You will be able to parallelise loops in C or C++ with OpenMP using reductions, scheduling clauses and data-sharing rules.
topics: Critical sections and atomics in OpenMP

nodes.name: Work & span
nodes.desc: The work-span model, parallelism and analysing parallel algorithms.
nodes.summary: You will be able to analyse parallel algorithms with the work-span model and compute their available parallelism.

nodes.name: Map, reduce & scan
nodes.desc: Parallel map, reduce, prefix sum and stencil patterns.
nodes.summary: You will be able to implement parallel map, reduce, prefix sum and stencil patterns and analyse their work and span.

nodes.name: Parallel sorting
nodes.desc: Parallel merge sort, sample sort and bitonic sort.
nodes.summary: You will be able to implement and analyse parallel merge sort, sample sort and bitonic sort.

nodes.name: MPI
nodes.desc: Message passing on clusters: point-to-point and collective operations.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write distributed programs with MPI using point-to-point messages and collective operations.

nodes.name: Parallel image filter
nodes.desc: Parallelise an image-processing pipeline and measure speedup across core counts.
nodes.summary: You will parallelise an image-processing pipeline and measure how speedup scales as you add cores.

nodes.name: SIMD
nodes.desc: Vector instructions, auto-vectorisation and intrinsics.
nodes.summary: You will be able to speed up loops with vector instructions through auto-vectorisation and intrinsics.

nodes.name: GPU programming
nodes.desc: The GPU execution model, kernels, threads, blocks and warps.
nodes.summary: You will understand the GPU execution model and be able to write kernels organised into threads, blocks and warps.

nodes.name: GPU memory
nodes.desc: Global, shared and register memory, coalescing and occupancy.
nodes.summary: You will be able to optimise GPU kernels by using the memory hierarchy well, coalescing accesses and tuning occupancy.

nodes.name: N-body on the GPU
nodes.desc: Implement an N-body simulation on the GPU and compare it against a multicore CPU version.
nodes.summary: You will implement an N-body simulation on the GPU and compare its performance against a multicore CPU version.
